title: Answer: time is the orientation and duration of a timelike conserved current

statements.text: Time is the order and duration that a non-vanishing, future-directed timelike conserved current carries. Clocks read that recovered duration, and global simultaneity holds only where the current's temporal one-form integrates to a foliation.

sources.quote: The completed Chronoflux Atlas recovers physical time from conserved continuity.
Where vorticity obstructs such a foliation, invariant duration along the flow remains well defined, as such, while one global simultaneity convention does not.
